title: Doctrine and climate — the two registers that stand beside the ladder
description: NEITHER IS EMITTED BY A DIAMOND, and that is the point (v0.230.0). Doctrine is 'universally applicable' — every inquiry at every scale is subject to it, so it belongs to no scale. Climate 'will apply to you regardless of your choice', so giving it a diamond would invent a maker for something the world makes. Both GROW rather than complete: 'the more you play the game then the more forms of doctrine you'll discover.' That is why the 2026-04 audit's coverage ratios against a fixed denominator were unscoreable — the sets are open by design, and no percentage of them can be computed.

last_reviewed.description: YYYY-MM-DD of the last doctrine retrospective. READ AS A FIRING CONDITION: a retrospective is DUE when a diamond has entered completed_diamonds with a completed_at later than this date. 'Learn these continuously' is not a trigger, and an un-triggered retrospective is the shape that has failed repeatedly in this project — so the trigger is an event that already gets recorded, not a calendar.

doctrine.description: What this project has learned applies universally to its own work. GROWS; never completes. An empty register is honest for a young project.

principle.description: Stated so it can be applied without further interpretation. 'Don't pick and choose, apply them all' — a principle held selectively is not doctrine.

learned_from.description: The concrete thing that changed and prompted this — 'look for what has changed and always ask why?'. A principle with no incident behind it was imported, not learned, and should say so here.

universal.description: Wardley's own split: doctrine is universally applicable, gameplay is context-specific. Set false and it is not doctrine — move it.

superseded_by.description: Doctrine may be replaced as the project learns. Supersede in place; do not delete, because the reason it was believed is the learning.

climate.description: Forces that apply regardless of choice. What an inquiry emits FROM climate is a DATED PREDICTION — which is what makes a climate entry scoreable later, and an undated one merely an opinion about the weather.

prediction.description: What this force implies will happen, stated so it can be wrong.

as_of.description: YYYY-MM-DD the prediction was made. Required: a prediction that cannot go stale cannot be scored, and an unscoreable prediction is not evidence.

horizon.description: When it should be checked. Optional, but a prediction with no horizon tends never to be read again.

outcome.description: Scored at the doctrine retrospective. 'unclear' is a real answer and beats forcing a verdict; 'unscored' means nobody has looked yet and must not be read as 'held'.
